title: 5 Weeks Post Op Breast Augmentation What to Expect
meta_description: 5 Weeks Post Op Breast Augmentation What to Expect: Learn about swelling, pain levels, activity limits, and healing milestones in your recovery.
excerpt: At 5 weeks after breast augmentation, most swelling has eased, but implants can still sit high and chest work still waits. Here is what's normal, how to sleep, which bra to wear, and the signs that mean you should call your surgeon.
quick_answer:
What should I expect 5 weeks after breast augmentation?

At 5 weeks most swelling has gone down: The Aesthetic Society says most residual swelling resolves within a month. Implants can still sit high and feel firm while they drop and fluff. Cleveland Clinic advises no heavy lifting for at least 4 weeks, says sports may take up to 6, and puts full recovery at about 6 to 8 weeks.

images.text_in_image:
Week 5 After Breast Augmentation: What's Normal
Swelling: Mostly gone. Most resolves within a month
Tightness: Common and easing
Drop and fluff: Implants may still sit high
Nerves: Tingling or shooting pains can last a few months
Scars: Still visible. Protect from the sun with SPF 30
Activity: Walking yes. Chest work not yet
Sources: The Aesthetic Society, University of Utah Health, MedlinePlus.
images.alt: Card titled Week 5 After Breast Augmentation: What's Normal. Swelling is mostly gone, and most resolves within a month. Tightness is common and easing. With drop and fluff, implants may still sit high. Tingling or shooting pains can last a few months. Scars are still visible, so protect them from the sun with SPF 30. Walking is fine and chest work is not yet. Sources: The Aesthetic Society, University of Utah Health and MedlinePlus.

5 Weeks Post-Op: Call Your Surgeon If
Fever or chills
Spreading redness or heat
Pus or bad-smelling drainage
An incision that opens
One breast suddenly swells
Severe pain your medicine doesn't help
Chest pain or trouble breathing: emergency room
Sources: Cleveland Clinic, MedlinePlus, UW Medicine.

sources.title: Breast Augmentation - Aftercare & Recovery
quotes: It typically takes one to two weeks to recover from a breast augmentation.
Most residual swelling will resolve within a month.
If the pain is extreme or long-lasting, contact your surgeon.
If you have external sutures, your surgeon will remove them in about a week. If your surgeon used tissue glue or tape, it will fall off on its own in a week or two.

Rest and sleep on your back in an inclined position (25-to 45-degree angle) for the initial postoperative days or if you have significant swelling. Use wedge pillows with an incline design or sleep in a recliner chair.
